brief.headline: Close the 16.6% gap on PET bottles to match Suraj Blow Plast's ₹1.87/NOS, and tighten payment to 15 days in exchange for a 10% price cut — freeing up ₹46539 cash for us.

priceAsk.summary: Cut the PET bottle price by 16.6% to match our best supplier, Suraj Blow Plast, at ₹1.87/NOS
priceAsk.target: ₹1.87/NOS on PET BOT AMBER 100ML/25MM NECK 12.5G SKU (saving ₹28644 annually)
priceAsk.basis: We pay them ₹2.18/NOS but Suraj Blow Plast delivers the same bottle at ₹1.87/NOS — a 16.6% gap. Market research shows fair pricing for caps at ₹0.85–0.95/pc with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at volume, so there's room to move.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move payment from 30 days to 15 days after receipt, in return for a 10% price cut
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Frees up ₹46539 for us; the 10% cut is roughly what paying 15 days early is worth to them (they borrow at 10.27%)

brief.financialLeverage: TPAC is financially solid — they made ₹637.48 Cr in revenue and keep ₹3.8 of every ₹100 they sell, with an [ICRA] A / Stable rating and light debt (0.19x). But their cash is tied up for 79 days (same as peers at 79d), and they pay suppliers in just 17 days versus a peer norm of 33d — so cash is somewhat tight. We're tiny to them at 0.02% of their sales, which limits our pull — but their grey-zone health score (62/100), GST filing delays, and EPF payment delays suggest fragility under the surface. We can push on price by benchmarking Suraj and using alternates, but keep the tone constructive to avoid tipping a supplier already showing stress signs.

evidence.point: We overpay them 16.6% on PET bottles versus our best supplier
They're a ₹637.48 Cr company — we're just 0.02% of their sales
evidence.figure: Our spend ₹11.32 L; their revenue ₹637.48 Cr; our share 0.02%

evidence.point: They borrow money at about 10.27%, so early payment is worth that much to them
They pay suppliers in 17 days but peers take 33 days — they're short on cash runway
Their health score is in the grey zone and they've delayed GST and EPF filings
evidence.figure: Health score B (62/100); Altman Z 2.77 (grey zone); risk flags: GST filing delays, EPF payment delays

evidence.point: Market research shows PP caps typically ask ₹0.85–0.95/pc, with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at volume
evidence.figure: Market ask band ₹0.55–1.20/pc; typical ₹0.85–0.95/pc; verdict MARKET-FAIR with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter at ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health score B (65/100) — a proven second source for pharma bottles and caps

alternates.name: Pearl Polymers Ltd
alternates.why: Listed PET bottle and jar specialist (Pearlpet brand) — a direct fit for our PET bottle needs

alternates.name: IVL Dhunseri Petrochem Industries Private Limited (East India)
alternates.why: A lead to qualify (verify before RFQ): manufacturer in East India; medium confidence from public web research

risks: We're only 0.02% of their revenue — on our own we have little leverage; consider bundling more SKUs or committing volume over multiple years to strengthen our hand
Their grey-zone health score (2.77 Altman Z), GST and EPF filing delays signal stress — pushing too hard could destabilize a supplier already showing cracks; keep the ask firm but constructive
They pay suppliers in 17 days (peers take 33d) and their cash is tied up for 79 days — asking for faster payment from us may meet resistance unless we trade it clearly for a price cut

No pricing data from us on average or best prices across rigid plastic packaging — the ₹28644 saving is only on one PET bottle SKU; validate the gap holds across other items before generalizing the ask
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to close the 16.6% gap on PET bottles to match Suraj Blow Plast's ₹1.87 price, and we're ready to move payment to 15 days in return for a 10% cut — that trade frees up cash for both of us.
